full_judgment:
7. The learned Advocate for the appellants argued that the defendant is claiming over the suit property by dint of a deed dated 22.02.1958 and the plaintiff is to seek relief by a declaration of title, thus the suit itself is not maintainable. Referring 33 DLR (AD) 286 he argued that if title is extinguished, declaration of title is a necessary. The plaintiff is to secure his title by a declaration and further submitted that if the amendment is allowed the parties shall be given an opportunity to cross examine as to such amendment and it should go on remand. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the respondents submitted that there is no explanation as to non-filing of the original purchase deed dated 22.02.1958 of the defendant No. 1, certified copy of which was marked exhibit-1 without any explanation regarding the original and why it could not produce before the Court and it is the only document by which the defendant is claiming ownership. 

 9. He further argued that by amendment all the co-sharers were made parties and also sought for a declaration that the deed dated 22.02.1958 ext-1 is void. The amendment was allowed without any objection in this revision application. By referring 45 DLR 15 he has submitted that the ext-1 being secondary evidence, in the absence of primary evidence by producing the original deed and without any explanation for non-filing of the original deed, the trial Court acted illegally in admitting ext-1. 

 10. The plaintiff in the revisional application having sought for amendment in the form of declaration of title and further declaration that the deed that 22.02.1956 (exhibit-1) be declared void, all the co-sharers having been made parties the prayer for amendment has been allowed without objection from the defendant. The trial Court also found that the plaintiff is the owner in possession of .50 acres of land and is entitled to have separate saham of this piece of land and also found that the plaintiff was successful in proving that at the time of alleged execution of the deed dated 22.02.1958 the defendant No. 1 Nazimuddin Sarder was insane and the trial Court found that the original deed dated 22.02.1958 was not produced nor any explanation was assigned in Court and that the certified copy thereof was not at all proved and further found that the deed dated 22.02.1958 is forged, fraudulent and without consideration which did not create any title or possession in favour of the defendant No. 1 or his sons and the lower appellate Court did not reverse the findings of the trial Court, the original deed dated 22.02.1985 was not produced in the Court and could not be proved by the defendants; that Court of Appeal below has not considered the material evidence, which were considered by the trial Court and without considering that the defendant No. 1 failed to produce the original deed dated 22.02.1958 revered the decision of the trial Court; that it would appear from the order No. 13 dated 04.08.1982 passed by the Munsif, 6th Court, Barisal in Title Suit No. 207 of 1981 that the plaintiff filed an application for interrogatories and from order No. 16 dated 20.01.1983 of the same Court it would appear that the defendant filed a petition praying for exemption from filing reply to the interrogatories stating in the petition ‘নম্বর মোকদ্দমায় অত্র পক্ষ বর্ণনা দিয়া পক্ষাভাব দোষের কথা উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন এক্ষেণ নথি তরজমা করিয়া দেখা যায় এই মোকদ্দমার আর কোন পক্ষ নাই’  and the defendant is estopped from taking the plea that Ratan Ali Sarder was not made party in the suit and therefore, the judgment and decree of the Court of Appeal below was not sustainable in law. 

 11. It appears that Exhibit-1 is the certified copy. There is no explanation of whereabouts of the original deed in their written statement. P.W.’s 1, 2 and 3 stated and asserted that executant of the document was mentally ill before his death. Thus, it is the vital and basic document to show the disposition by Nazimuddin Sarder, the admitted owner which was not produced and there is also no explanation. It appears that the plaintiff in the instant revisional application has sought for amendment in the form of declaration of title and also made prayer that the deed is to be declared void and further all the co-sharers were made parties and those have been allowed without any objection from the defendant. In this particular case ext. 1 the deed dated 22.02.1958 is a vital document and was not produced nor there was any explanation as to what has happened to the original deed, therefore, it supports the positive assertion of the plaintiff that Nazimuddin was insane at a time when it was allegedly executed and accordingly the same was declared as a forged one. The amendment was allowed without any objection. Therefore, it is not necessary to send it on remand as amendment can be allowed at any stage. Moreso, when the amendment was the subject matter of admitted fact and no objection was raised regarding the subject matter at the material time.
